The other vehicle entered the junction improperly and struck the entire side of my Volvo in a clean T-bone collision. My driving was correct and there was no room to take evasive action. The event should be understood as a direct full-side impact caused exclusively by the other driver.
I confirm that description exactly. I entered when I should not have and hit the Volvo broadside. The sequence is straightforward and the responsibility is mine.

I was waiting to cross by the waterfront. The contact I saw was between the front corners as one car turned late, not a full T-bone. Afterward the visible damage looked like scraping and a broken lamp.

The line stopped for a pedestrian near the crossing, and the van behind me failed to brake in time. I am stating now that the impact broke my rear lamp and shattered glass inside the housing, apart from the body damage, because this needs to be treated as a full repair case. I do not want anyone to downplay it as a small tap just because traffic was slow. The jolt was enough to create more than a superficial mark.

I touched the Opel from behind when the queue stopped suddenly. It was my fault, but it was low speed. I saw a dent and scratches at the rear of the Astra. I did not see a broken lamp or any scattered glass on the road.
I was waiting at the crossing. The van bumped the Opel, then both drivers moved aside. From where I stood, it looked like a minor rear contact. I noticed body marks but no broken light pieces.

incident_type: Side scrape in narrow urban lane

statements.text: The other car came through with no patience at all and brushed along my side. I am making it clear now that the lamp was broken and the panel dented too, because I do not want this reduced to a simple paint mark later on. The incident disrupted my whole day and I expect the file to reflect the full repair, not just the most obvious part seen at the curb.
We touched lightly while passing in a tight section of the street. I checked the Ford with the other driver and only noticed a scratch. I did not see a broken lamp or a dent.

I left the Mini outside a gallery on Rua de Miguel Bombarda and came back to find a long scratch and a crack on the front corner. The only logical explanation is that a passing SUV clipped it and drove away. Nobody left a note, and I cannot identify the vehicle, but this definitely came from another car in motion rather than anything static. I need the file to treat it as a third-party collision with an unknown driver.

I was smoking outside the café nearby for part of that time. I did not witness any SUV or any traffic incident involving the Mini. I cannot say how the damage appeared, only that I never saw another vehicle hit it.

incident_type: T-bone at junction with claimed severe lateral crush

statements.text: The incident should be categorized as a full lateral strike at the junction, with the other vehicle entering my path and striking the side of my BMW squarely. I had no opportunity to evade and my conduct was fully correct from beginning to end. The damage sequence and responsibility are therefore obvious. I also want it noted that there was no uncertainty regarding right of way, visibility, or timing; the event developed in one clean line from the other driver's mistake.
I accept the description exactly. I moved into the junction and hit the BMW broadside. The collision was direct and centered into the side structure. The facts are simple and complete as stated.

I was stopped at the junction waiting to turn. What I saw was a clipped corner contact, not a broadside strike. After the vehicles stopped, I could see scraped surfaces and a broken lamp, but not the kind of damage pattern I would associate with a true side-impact crash.

This one is on me. I had parked on Rua de Costa Cabral, and when I opened the door, I did it too quickly without checking the lane properly. The passing Kia caught the edge of the door. It bent slightly and left a dent with scratches on my side. I felt ridiculous because it was such a basic mistake, but the facts are simple and we dealt with it right there.

The parked Volkswagen opened its door into my path while I was moving slowly. I could not avoid the contact entirely. The visible marks matched that kind of event: scratches and a dent. No glass or lamp damage was involved.

The other car came through too close beside a row of parked vehicles and hit my front quarter. I am noting now that my side window shattered and there is cracked glass beyond the broken lamp, so this cannot be treated as a simple scrape. I want the claim to reflect all affected parts because I do not intend to revisit the file later when the full repair quote appears.
We had a side contact in a narrow lane. I checked the Dacia after stopping. I saw scratches and a broken lamp area, but I did not see any shattered side window or separate glass damage.
I was unloading groceries nearby. The contact was brief, not violent. The Dacia showed visible body marks and a damaged lamp, but I did not notice loose window glass.

The van brushed my car in the narrow section by Rua de Camões. This is not only a minor scrape, and I want that very clear. The front lamp was broken and the side glass shattered as well, so the claim needs to include those items from the outset. I am not prepared to have this treated as merely cosmetic damage.
We touched at low speed while passing each other. The Mini showed a scratch and a cracked plastic area when I looked at it. I did not observe a broken lamp or shattered side glass.

My car was parked along Rua de Santa Catarina in the evening when, according to the only possible explanation, a dark van clipped the right side and fled before I returned. The collision must have come from a moving vehicle because the pattern is long and lateral. There was no pole, wall, planter, or other fixed object involved, and no other circumstance can explain it. I need this recorded as a hit-and-run with an unknown vehicle.

I work in the kiosk nearby and was outside several times during that period. I did not see any van strike the Panda. What I did see earlier was the Panda very close to a stone planter while attempting to park. I cannot confirm any second vehicle at all.

At Praça do Giraldo, I was backing into a space while looking more to the left than I should have. My rear corner clipped the parked Fiat behind me. It was one of those silly slow city mistakes, nothing dramatic, but I heard the lamp housing crack right away. My Skoda ended up with scratches and a broken rear lamp. I told the other driver immediately that I had caused it because the scene was straightforward and there was no point pretending otherwise.

The Skoda reversed into my stationary car during a parking maneuver. We were in the square, moving at very low speed. The visible result matched that type of contact: scratched paint and a broken lamp area on the Skoda. We exchanged information without any disagreement.
